questions.question:
The two statements below are followed by three conclusions labeled I, II and III. Assuming that the information in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with generally established facts, decide which conclusion(s) logically and definitely follow(s) from the information given in the statements. 

**Statements:** 

1. Some mangoes are fruits. 

2. All fruits are sweets. 

**Conclusions:** 

I. Some sweets are mangoes. 

II. All sweets are fruits. 

III. Some mangoes are neither fruits nor sweets.

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusion I follows

questions.solution:
Here the logic is:

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/37d1fb5e2fd37d460519ad766535460c3b0e68e8bdd27090ad7fceff2b8315f1.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. Some sweets are mangoes → **True** (As "some fruits are mangoes and all fruits are sweets" so, the overlapping part of mangoes and fruit will be sweets hence, true)

II. All sweets are fruits → **False** (as "all fruits are sweets" means fruits is a subset of Sweets but all sweets are fruit is a possible condition ( when fruit and sweets exactly overlap each other) but not definite hence, false)

III. Some mangoes are neither fruits nor sweets. → **False** (as "some fruits are mangoes and all fruits are sweets" here nothing is mentioned where remaining part are neither fruit nor sweet, this is a possible condition not definite, Hence false)

Hence, **"Only conclusion I follow"** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea728f908b060e4db8cdc0f37188bd8bacc49aff99cc89b07517095538ec56de.png] 

There is a possibility that all mangoes are Fruits, so in that case the given conclusion will be invalid. If any conclusion is true in all the possible cases, then only that conclusion is considered as true.

I. Some robots are boys.

III. Some robots are girls.

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow.
Only conclusion III follows.
All conclusions I, II and III follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible venn diagram is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a3db8bfcc4d2b78fb4974a2d5d6c53ed091fa31133fd205cfa6b838d3038c5c8.png]

questions.question:
Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All towels are cloths.

No cloth is a blanket.

Some blankets are cushions.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some towels are cushions.

II. No cushion is a cloth.

III. No towel is a blanket.

options.text: Only conclusion III follows.
Only conclusion I follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn Diagram is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7307bd6cd27867b48fc90a948995ef88091b131c05323c61373065474ab41301.png] 

**I. Some towels are cushions → False ( **In the statement it is stated that all towels are clothes and there is no relation between cloth and cushion therefore there is no relation between towels and cushion. It is possible but not definite. Thus,** the conclusion I does not follows.)**

**II. No cushion is a cloth **→ False** (**There is no such evidence that gives us the information about cloth not being related to cushion and therefore it us a possibility that cushion relates to cloth. It is possible but not definite. Thus, **the conclusion does not follow.)**

**III. No towel is a blanket **→ True** (**In the statement it is clearly said that "all towels are cloths" and "no cloth is a blanket" therefore it is safe to say that there is no relation between towel and blanket. Thus, **the conclusion follows.)**

Hence, the correct answer is** "Only conclusion III follows".**
